explanation: In 1878 Eadweard Muybridge used a row of cameras to show that a galloping horse has all four hooves off the ground at once. The Lumières' paid show in Paris came in 1895.

claims.text: Eadweard Muybridge photographed a galloping horse in sequence in June 1878.
The Lumière brothers held their first paid public film screening in Paris on 28 December 1895.
Muybridge's photographs showed that a galloping horse has all four hooves off the ground at one point in its stride.
Muybridge used a row of cameras, triggered in turn as the horse passed.

writerNotes: Self-check 9.3. Lint: clean. Claims: every claim listed, risk at or above the C26 floor and raised where a detail is easy to get wrong; the schema's riskReason list has no 'only' or 'counterintuitive', so such claims carry the nearest listed reason. Datasets: no pinned dataset covers film or TV facts, so every high-risk claim here needs checker evidence from the web. Rival test: Arguing for the Lumières: their screening is the famous birth of cinema, but Muybridge's sequence photographs came 17 years earlier. Volatility: evergreen; no time words; nothing depends on events after mid-2026. Regional: two founding moments of cinema, from the US and France. Style: Oxford spelling, straight single quotes, plain hyphens, explanation of 33 words. Myths: claims screened against myths.json; no claim resembles a listed myth. Mystery and encore: not applicable to a practice item. Doubts: c2 is worded 'first paid public screening' because the Lumières showed films privately earlier in 1895; the label says 'first paid'.
